sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of Sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the southeastern edge of Hopewell borough beyond East Prospect along Princeton Avenue, which the sheet also calls Union. East Prospect runs down the left edge of the part. 2nd Street and 1st Street cross Maple Avenue and Princeton Avenue, and the borough line with Hopewell Township follows 1st Street and then turns along the bottom of the sheet. Blocks 51, 108, 109, 111 and 112 are drawn mostly as open lots with a few frame dwellings, autos and coops along East Prospect and Princeton Avenue. The Second Calvary Baptist Church stands on 1st Street at Princeton Avenue, and the Hopewell Grammar School, a large brick building heated by steam, stands south of Princeton Avenue on the borough line. East of 1st Street, in block 110 in the township, a dashed drive leads from Princeton Avenue to St. Michael's Orphanage Industrial Schools. The complex has classrooms and dormitories, a chapel, a laundry and boiler house, a water tower and several sheds, and an arrow notes the barns 1000 feet away. Those farm buildings are drawn in a separate inset at the bottom right of the sheet, which is not part of this annotation. The upper half of the sheet holds the key map, the street and specials index and notes on water facilities and the fire department. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Maple Av. is South Maple Street in OpenStreetMap.
Princeton Av. is labelled with the older name Union in brackets.
Drawn at 100 ft to an inch; the first pass fitted 4.17 px/ft against about 4.04 from the printed scale bar, and the second pass held it to the atlas scale (moved 16 m).

Top half: key map (600 ft to an inch, approx.), index, water and fire notes (not configured). Bottom half at 100 ft to an inch: part 1 E. Prospect St, 2nd St, 1st St, Maple Av, Princeton Av (Union) with St. Michael's Orphanage Industrial Schools; part 2 inset bottom right: St. Michael's Orphanage farm buildings ('1000 ft to barns'). North to the left.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the blocks east of East Broad in the north of Hopewell borough, between East Broad on the left and East Prospect on the right, with Columbia Avenue running up the middle of the sheet. Maple Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally, and Princeton Avenue, also named Union, runs along the bottom edge. The blocks are numbered 10, 11, 105 and 106 and are almost entirely residential: frame dwellings, most of two storeys, with autos, coops and small sheds behind them, laid out on long narrow lots facing Columbia Avenue and East Broad. A brook, drawn in blue, crosses the upper left corner of the sheet near East Broad, and the land between it and Columbia Avenue is largely open. The only institution on the sheet is St. Alphonsus Roman Catholic Church at the corner of Princeton Avenue and East Prospect, heated by furnace and lit by electricity. Four-inch water pipes run in East Broad, Columbia Avenue and East Prospect, and fire hydrants stand at the corners. The sheet adjoins Sheet 5 at the top, where an inset carries the three streets on to Elm Avenue, Sheet 3 below Princeton Avenue, and Sheet 1 beyond East Prospect. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Maple Av. is South Maple Street in OpenStreetMap.
E. Broad St, Columbia Av, E. Prospect St, Maple Av, Princeton Av (Union). 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the business centre of Hopewell borough on the east side of East Broad, between Princeton Avenue at the top and South Greenwood Avenue at the bottom, with Columbia Avenue and East Prospect running up the sheet and Seminary Avenue crossing it. Hamilton Avenue and Blackwell Avenue are drawn as short stubs entering from the left across East Broad, and the corner of North Greenwood Avenue and West Broad Street appears at the bottom left. Along East Broad between Seminary Avenue and South Greenwood Avenue stand the commercial buildings of the town: stores, a tinning and plumbing shop, a bake house, an auto repair shop, the Central Hotel Apartments and the Post Office. Behind them are the Calvary Baptist Church and the brick Public School with its school rooms and a fire siren on a steel tower. The rest of the sheet, along Columbia Avenue and East Prospect, is residential, with frame dwellings, autos and coops on deep lots in blocks 6, 7, 8 and 9. A large brick building at the top right belongs to the next sheet. Water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets, with hydrants at the corners. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: The junction of East Broad, West Broad, North Greenwood and South Greenwood is at the bottom left of the sheet.
E. Broad, Columbia Av, E. Prospect, Princeton Av, Seminary Av, S. Greenwood Av; Hamilton and Blackwell Av stubs. 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the blocks between the Philadelphia and Reading Railway and East Broad in the north of Hopewell borough, from Hamilton Avenue at the top to North Greenwood Avenue at the bottom. Lafayette Avenue runs up the middle of the sheet and Blackwell Avenue crosses it; Railroad Place and Cook Avenue run between Blackwell Avenue and North Greenwood Avenue near the tracks, and Somerset runs off the top left towards Sheet 9. Industry lines the railway on the left: the Hopewell Valley Canning Company with its canning, soldering, storage and packing rooms, the J. B. Hill and Son coal, lumber, grain and feed yard with a coal trestle, the Hopewell Chocolate Company, a freight house and the brick passenger station of the P. and R. Railway. Railroad Place has stores, a garage for fourteen cars and a printing shop. The rest of the sheet is residential, with frame dwellings on Lafayette Avenue, Hamilton Avenue and Blackwell Avenue. Public buildings include the Hopewell M. E. Church on Blackwell Avenue, the Free Public Library on East Broad, and a bank at the corner of East Broad and North Greenwood Avenue. Stores and a garage stand at the top right corner by East Broad. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Lafayette Av. is Lafayette Street in OpenStreetMap; Cook Av. is Cook Place.
Railroad Place is also labelled Railroad Avenue in brackets.
The junction of East Broad and Hamilton Avenue was detected 17 m off the fit and rejected.
Hamilton Av, Lafayette Av, Blackwell Av, E. Broad, Cook Av, Railroad Pl, N. Greenwood; Hopewell Valley Canning Co, J.B. Hill & Son, Hopewell Chocolate Co, P&R depot. 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of Sheet 5 covers the northwest corner of Hopewell borough between East Broad and Front, north of North Greenwood Avenue, with Burton Avenue crossing the sheet. A brook, drawn in blue, runs diagonally across the whole part under a bridge on Burton Avenue. North of Burton Avenue the land is largely open, with the borough pumping station, a well house and two wells, a pump house and an eight-inch pipe that runs about 3550 feet to the reservoir. Acton Court, an arbitrary name, is lettered on the left edge with a few dwellings, and an arrow points to a dwelling and farm buildings 300 feet away. South of Burton Avenue the Hopewell Products Company makes toys in a two-storey frame building beside the brook. Along Front and North Greenwood Avenue there are frame dwellings with autos and coops, and a private driveway runs into block 52 from North Greenwood Avenue. Hart Avenue and Golden Avenue are lettered as stubs on the far side of North Greenwood Avenue. The railway lies beyond Front on the right, where section houses and the passenger station are drawn at the edge, and a steel and concrete bridge is noted in the bottom right corner. Much of the left side is marked vacant beyond. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Acton Ct. is labelled as an arbitrary name.
Hart Avenue, Golden Avenue and Front at North Greenwood Avenue were hand-picked: the detector did not find these T junctions with stub or one-sided streets.

Part 1: Burton Av, Front St, N. Greenwood Av, Driveway, Acton Ct, brook, pumping station. Part 2: inset at top, E. Broad, Columbia Av and E. Prospect at Elm Av (north end of sheet 2). 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-5-2.description: The inset at the top of Sheet 5, separated from the main part by a heavy line, carries the north end of Sheet 2 on to Elm Avenue at the northern edge of Hopewell borough. East Broad, Columbia Avenue and East Prospect run up the inset and meet Elm Avenue along the top edge, where only the south side of Elm Avenue is drawn. The blocks are numbered 103, 105 and 106. They hold a few frame dwellings with autos, a wagon shed, coops and storage buildings on large lots, and a brook in blue runs through block 105 from a concrete bridge on Elm Avenue. A note on Columbia Avenue gives 195 feet to the borough line. Four-inch water pipes run in Elm Avenue, Columbia Avenue and East Prospect, and a hydrant stands at the corner of East Broad and Elm Avenue. A row of five small dwellings, lettered A to E, stands outside the inset frame on the right, in the main part of the sheet. The inset is drawn at the same scale and orientation as Sheet 2 and adjoins it along its lower edge. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Elm Av. is South Elm Street in OpenStreetMap.
Columbia Avenue and East Prospect at Elm Avenue were hand-picked: Elm Avenue is drawn with its south edge only.

Part 1: Burton Av, Front St, N. Greenwood Av, Driveway, Acton Ct, brook, pumping station. Part 2: inset at top, E. Broad, Columbia Av and E. Prospect at Elm Av (north end of sheet 2). 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of Sheet 6 covers the west side of Hopewell borough south of North Greenwood Avenue, on both sides of the Philadelphia and Reading Railway. Hart Avenue and Golden Avenue run down from North Greenwood Avenue and are crossed by Shaftesbury Avenue; Drake Avenue, marked not opened, runs beside the railway. The tracks cross the sheet from top to bottom with a steel and concrete bridge at North Greenwood Avenue and a coal trestle on a siding. East of the railway, along Model Avenue, are the lumber sheds, hay and grain storage and agricultural implement buildings of A. S. Golden, a block of apartments, a club house, a stable and the works of W. I. Reid, makers of concrete burial vaults. A row of dwellings lines Model Avenue down to Mercer Street at the bottom right, and Center Street is lettered entering from the right. West of the railway the blocks along Hart Avenue and Golden Avenue are residential, and block 55 is largely open, with an athletic field and grandstand and W. I. Reid's septic tank works at the bottom. The left edge is marked vacant beyond. The lower left corner is a separate inset of North Greenwood Avenue, not part of this annotation. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Shaftesbury Av. is Shaftsbury Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Drake Av. is marked not opened and is not in OpenStreetMap.

Part 1: N. Greenwood Av, Hart Av, Golden Av, Shaftesbury Av, Drake Av (not opened), P&R Ry, Model Av; A.S. Golden lumber, W.I. Reid vaults. Part 2: inset bottom left, N. Greenwood Av block 53 further west. 50 ft. North to the left.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: North Greenwood Avenue block 53 further west (lots 60 to 70) (no street junction; needs carried points from sheet-5-1 (opposite side of North Greenwood Avenue) or parcel corners).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the blocks between Model Avenue and West Broad in the centre of Hopewell borough, from North Greenwood Avenue and South Greenwood Avenue at the top to Mercer at the bottom. Center runs down from North Greenwood Avenue and turns to meet Model Avenue. Most of the sheet is taken by the cemetery in block 2, with a long storage shed, and by the First Baptist Church at its corner on West Broad. Along Mercer and Model Avenue stand the Hopewell House hotel with its stables and the burial vault works of W. I. Reid, with stone cutting and concrete storage. The right side of the sheet, across West Broad, has stores and dwellings, the Fire Department with a hall on the second floor, a printing shop, a paint and oil store, a tin shop and frame barns, and a brook in blue crosses it diagonally. Dwellings with brick linings and frame houses line North Greenwood Avenue and Center at the top. Water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets, with hydrants at the corners. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: The junction of Mercer and West Broad is placed 7.9 m apart on Sheets 7 and 8.
N. and S. Greenwood Av, Model Av, Center St, W. Broad, Mercer St; cemetery, 1st Baptist Church, fire dept. 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-8-1.description: The main part of Sheet 8 covers the southwest of Hopewell borough between Model Avenue and West Broad, south of Mercer. Louellen Avenue runs diagonally across the sheet from West Broad near Mercer to the bottom left, and North Lanning Avenue meets West Broad and South Lanning Avenue at the lower right. A brook runs along Mercer behind a row of stores, a tin shop, a bakery and a cement pipe works, and continues under a wooden bridge on Model Avenue into a swamp at the left edge. The First Presbyterian Church stands in block 5 between Louellen Avenue and West Broad. On Louellen Avenue is the saw and feed mill of A. G. Fetter, marked not in operation, with lumber sheds and a well. The rest of the sheet is residential, with frame dwellings, autos and sheds on Model Avenue, Louellen Avenue, West Broad and North Lanning Avenue, and the left edge is marked vacant. The inset of the Hopewell Creamery at the bottom of the sheet is not part of this annotation. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Louellen Av. is Louellen Street in OpenStreetMap.
The part fits with 3.6 m RMSE; no single junction explains it, and West Broad may be drawn slightly bent.
Part 1: Mercer St, Model Av, Louellen Av, W. Broad, N. and S. Lanning Av; 1st Presbyterian Church, A.G. Fetter saw mill. Part 2: inset bottom, Hopewell Creamery on Model Av. 50 ft. North to the left.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Hopewell Creamery on Model Avenue (no street junction; needs parcel or building corners on Model Avenue).

sheet-9-1.description: The main part of Sheet 9 covers the southwestern end of Hopewell borough along West Broad, south of North Lanning Avenue and South Lanning Avenue. West Broad runs down the sheet on the left, West Prospect runs parallel to it on the right, and Ege Avenue crosses between them. The blocks are numbered 57, 58, 117 and 118. The area is residential: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys, a few with tile or concrete block walls, with autos, coops and storage sheds behind them. A garage for sixteen cars stands on West Broad at the bottom left. Large parts of the blocks are open, and the land beyond is marked vacant on both sides. Four-inch water pipes run in South Lanning Avenue, West Prospect and Ege Avenue. The insets on the right side of the sheet, Somerset with the former factories of the E. B. Coy Manufacturing Company and the Smith Novelty Company, and West Prospect at Lawyer's Lane, are separate parts. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: The junction of West Broad with North and South Lanning Avenue is placed 5.1 m apart on Sheets 8 and 9.

Part 1: W. Broad, S. Lanning Av, Ege Av, W. Prospect. Part 2: inset upper right, Somerset St with E.B. Coy Mfg Co and Smith Novelty Co (north of sheet 4). Part 3: inset lower right, W. Prospect between Lawyer's Lane and S. Lanning Av. 50 ft. North to the left.

sheet-9-3.description: The inset at the lower right of Sheet 9, framed by heavy lines, shows West Prospect between South Lanning Avenue at the bottom and Lawyer's Lane at the top, at the southern edge of Hopewell borough. It continues West Prospect beyond the junction with South Lanning Avenue that the main part of the sheet shows at its top. Blocks 116 and 117 hold a few frame dwellings of one and two storeys with autos, a coop and a storage building, on large lots, and the land beyond is marked vacant. Lawyer's Lane is drawn 33 feet wide and West Prospect 50 feet. A four-inch water pipe runs in South Lanning Avenue with a hydrant at the corner. The inset is drawn at the same scale as the rest of the sheet with its own north arrow. North is to the left of the page, so the streets that run up the page run roughly east-northeast on the ground.
notes: Placed with a two-point helmert from the junctions at each end of West Prospect; low confidence.
Lawyer's Lane is the service road Lawyers Lane in OpenStreetMap.
